chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr and Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan and Ibn Abi 'Umayr all from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

Ihram (entering the state of consecration) is not valid except after a prescribed prayer; you enter ihram after it following the final salutation, and if it is a voluntary prayer, you pray two rak'ahs and enter ihram after it following the salutation.

When you have finished your prayer, praise Allah, extol Him, and send blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and say: 'O Allah, I ask You to make me among those who answered You, believed in Your promise, and followed Your command, for I am Your servant and in Your grip; I am protected only by what You protect, and I take only what You give. You have mentioned Hajj, so I ask You to strengthen me for it upon Your Book and the Sunnah of Your Prophet, and to empower me for what I am weak in, and to accept my rituals from me with ease and health from You, and make me among Your guests whom You were pleased with, chose, named, and decreed.'

O Allah, then perfect for me my Hajj and Umrah. O Allah, I intend the Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj) with Umrah until Hajj, upon Your Book and the Sunnah of Your Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). If something befalls me that detains me, then release me where you detained me, according to the decree You have decreed upon me.

O Allah, if it is not a Hajj, then let it be an Umrah. Let my hair, skin, flesh, blood, bones, marrow, and sinews be in Ihram for You, from women, clothing, and perfume, seeking Your Countenance and the Last Home by that.

He (peace be upon him) said: 'And it suffices you to say this once when you enter Ihram. Then stand and walk slowly. When the earth is level with you, whether you are walking or riding, then say Talbiyah.'

key_terms.التَّمَتُّعُ: Tamattu' (a type of Hajj combining Umrah and Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What is the proper method and supplication for entering Ihram according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the juristic preference (mustahabb) of performing Ihram immediately following a prayer, emphasizing spiritual readiness through specific supplications. The detailed du'a highlights key Shia theological concepts such as divine decree (Qadr) and the intention for Tamattu', while the instruction to walk briefly before reciting the Talbiyah reflects the practical etiquette of transitioning from prayer to pilgrimage rites.
